text: If she wants to cheat, she will cheat. And if she is loyal, she will stay loyal, even in a club, with male friends, or on a girl's trip. This is the argument I keep hearing from people who say that if you don't let your girlfriend do whatever she wants, you are insecure, controlling, or lack confidence. On the surface, this argument sounds reasonable. And to be clear, I actually agree with part of it. If a woman truly wants to cheat, she will cheat no matter what you do. No rules, no control, no restrictions will stop someone who already made that decision. But here where it gets more complicated. What if she doesn't want to cheat? What if she is generally a loyal girlfriend? Does that mean she will stay loyal no matter the situation, no matter the environment, no matter the people around her? And by the way, to be fair to the ladies, the logic I'm about to present applies to men as well. You see, for many people, cheating is not a simple on or off switch. It's not zero or one. It's a gradient. There are situations where the chances are lower, and situations where the chances are much higher. Being at a library studying is not the same as being at a bar or a club without your partner, with alcohol involved and environment being very loose. Let me give you a real story I heard from someone else. There was a guy with a very loyal girlfriend. Let's call her Anna. Good relationship, trust, love, everything. Anna had single girlfriends, and one of them decided to celebrate her birthday abroad at a resort. At first, Anna didn't want to go, but her friends convinced her. Her boyfriend trusted her and said, fine. Anna tried to do everything right. She sent pictures, they talked, and had video calls. On a birthday night, the girls wanted to go out. Anna didn't want to drink, didn't want to party, but again, her friends pushed her. Then alcohol got involved. A group of guys approached. Anna said she had a boyfriend and was about to leave, but the girl said, relax, everything will be fine. Just stay with us. One thing led to another, they went to another venue, and that night Anna cheated. So what's the moral of the story? Yes, if someone wants to cheat, they will cheat. But even people who don't want to cheat can end up cheating when the environment, pressure, and circumstances line up. There is no foolproof way to protect your relationship from that, but there are ways to reduce the risk. And having clear boundaries is one of them.
